issues.description: Method name mismatch for Stock.add-to-stock operation: The problem statement UML and the reference solution expect a method Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template Stock class instead declares public void addItem(StockIngredient). This naming inconsistency means code that follows the UML or the solution (which calls addToStockIngredients) will not compile against the provided template, and students may be confused which method name to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or (B) add a small forwarding method in the template: public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient i) { addItem(i); }. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML and the solution to use addItem consistently. Prefer matching the UML/solution by adding addToStockIngredients to the template to avoid breaking the instructional materials.

issues.description: The concept is adding a StockIngredient into the Stock's internal collection. The problem statement / UML names this operation addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template Stock class implements this operation as addItem(StockIngredient). The solution Stock class implements addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). Because the UML and problem description use addToStockIngredients but the starter code exposes addItem, students may be unable to directly map the required API to the provided template, increasing cognitive load and risking incorrect edits (e.g., implementing the UML method while the template already has a differently named implementation).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template's API with the UML/problem statement by renaming the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). Alternatively, add a small forwarding method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the template that delegates to addItem to preserve any existing internal naming while matching the documented API. This makes the template consistent with the UML and the solution and removes the identifier-mapping burden from students.
